title: Literal sparks fly between two rare lives in Take Charge of My Heart - t2ONLINE

Take Charge of My Heart Review: Chae Soo-bin & Kim Young-kwang's Electrifying K-Drama | Netflix | t2ONLINE

 Screen Literal sparks fly between two rare lives in Take Charge of My Heart
 By Ankita Chandra 
 Published: 2 Nov 2026, 12:09AM | 4 min read Kim Young-kwang and Chae Soo-bin star in Netflix’s Take Charge of My Heart
 Advertisement Genre : Fantasy, romance 
 Where to watch : Netflix 
 You will love it if you love: 
 Strangers-to-lovers arcs 
 Protagonists with creative careers  
 Self-reflexive narratives  
 Elite backdrops 
 Celebrity love triangles 
 t2 rating : 3/5 
 Sparks do fly between soulmates, and lovers do feel that their hearts are “recharged” when they spend quality time together. In Netflix’s Take Charge of My Heart , both these things happen, and quite literally so. A woman who possesses the ability to conduct electricity into the surrounding environment meets a man with an artificial heart powered by a battery that needs recharging every once in a while. Any passionate rom-com viewer can figure out the rest. Well, they come together, the problem is solved, and a happy ending comes right after.
 Probably this is the reason that, even amid the new trend of weekly episodes being released to maintain suspense, Netflix chose to drop all twelve episodes at one go. Not only is the plot easy enough to predict, but the series is actually based on a Naver Series webnovel titled Charge Me Up by Haebeon. A set of entertaining performances, thoughtfully curated frames that evoke the animated pages of webnovels, and some brilliant comic sequences bring an element of freshness to the otherwise predictable story, making the screen adaptation totally worth the watch, even if you are familiar with the original material.
 The series sees When the Phone Rings star Chae Soo-bin stepping into the shoes of Na Bo-bae, a successful screenwriter who has won multiple accolades but somehow still feels stuck in life while others accomplish milestone after milestone. Her sister is a gold medallist in Taekwondo, and her brother is a Judo pro. Bo-bae, however, is still struggling to compose the perfect romance for her director’s next project, failing which her contract with the company will not be renewed.
 The reason behind this is not just her non-existent love life, but also the fact that she is simply not capable of building one. After being struck by lightning in an open ground as a child, Bo-bae developed the rare ability to conduct electricity through her supercharged body into the surrounding environment and to the people she touched. This led to a life completely devoid of physical touch and, as a result, no long-term romantic relationships, as whoever she touched for too long would be shocked into unconsciousness.
 Right after learning about Bo-bae’s special ability, which is also her plea, the audience is introduced to Baek Ho-rang (Kim Young-kwang). A top executive at the luxurious resort and heir to the elite TS Group, Ho-rang is a man of action. However, his weak heart prevents him from being considered a long-term successor over his cousin. To do away with this physical obstacle, Ho-rang plans to undergo surgery, after which his artificial heart would be powered by a battery that, the doctor claims, would only lose its power after a century, making further replacement surgeries unnecessary. But the operation does not achieve total success, with the battery draining much faster than the doctor had surmised.
 Incidentally, Bo-bae is also admitted to the same hospital with appendicitis while Ho-rang is undergoing surgery and recovering, and the doctors observe that the battery in his artificial heart miraculously charges up when she is in close proximity. Meanwhile, Bo-bae discovers another important and beneficial detail: Ho-rang seems to be the only person who is immune to the electric shocks others experience on touching her.
 Noticing the miraculous effects of each other’s proximity, the two strike a deal. Bo-bae moves in with Ho-rang so that his heart can be safely charged whenever he needs it, while Ho-rang promises Bo-bae that he will equip her with enough romantic experience by being her “platonic” boyfriend, taking her out on dates and buying her flowers, thereby providing enough inspiration for her to complete the story for her screen project that could save her job.
 But their smooth road to real love and a happy ending is complicated by another player in the game. Ji Eun-ho (Cha Woo-min), the actor who got his breakthrough role in a production written by Bo-bae, is another contender for her attention, and Ho-rang’s jealousy leads to a number of comic scenes, adding an extra dose of entertainment to the series. A light-hearted fantasy premise, a celebrity’s intrusion into the primary romance and the resulting comedy make Take Charge of My Heart quite a refreshing watch if you are looking to unwind with a light-hearted yet unconventional romance.
 Characters we treasure… 
 Chae Soo-bin as Na Bo-bae:  
 What you notice instantly  as Bo-bae is introduced  in the first episode is how 
 perfectly she matches the  animated female writer  archetype. Her bushy  hair, nerdy glasses and  oversized hoodies remind  you of similar characters  illustrated in comic strips.  Soo-bin’s effortlessly  comic aura, which remains  consistent throughout  the series, adds to the  webnovel-like feel of the  story, resulting in a unique  portrayal. 
 Kim Young-kwang as Baek Ho-rang: 
 Ho-rang’s is a familiar  character in K-dramas: the  rich, confident and slightly  arrogant businessman  who is transformed into  a sweetheart in love.  Young-kwang portrays the  character with a subtle  eccentricity that makes  the distant CEO feel more  like a flesh-and-blood  human with his own  vulnerabilities, while also  keeping the comic element  intact.
